**Where sources disagree, every version is recorded here as an alternative, with its source. ## One phase figure: DIIG Fig. 1.1.1

The seven phases of "planning and implementing a digital health enterprise" have ONE source, the DIIG's own figure. The handbooks that print it are reproductions of it and cite it; they are not separate sources for it. Its SVG rendering is [`vfig-p017.svg`](../library/9789240010567-eng/figures/vfig-p017.svg) (bean `folio-assistant-70zt`). It is drawn from the DIIG PDF's own vector layer, never by hand, and records its source (the PDF's sha256, the page and the crop) in its `<metadata>`; `bun run smart-base:diig-figure:check` fails if the drawing is edited or the crop drifts.

> "The process of planning and implementing an appropriate digital health enterprise within the broader ecosystem includes several phases:"<br>— DIIG §1.1, PDF p.16 (printed p.4) (`9789240010567-eng/page-016`)

> "Fig. 1.1.1 outlines these steps as well as supporting resources"<br>— DIIG §1.1, Fig. 1.1.1, drawn on PDF p.17 (printed p.5) (`9789240010567-eng/page-016`)

The phases, in the DIIG's words:

1. assessing the current state and enabling environment
2. establishing a shared understanding and strategic planning
3. defining the future state
4. planning enterprise architecture
5. determining health content requirements
6. monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and fostering data use
7. implementing, maintaining and scaling

## Approaches recorded as alternatives

### Prioritizing bottlenecks: three criteria, with or without a summed score

DIIG Chapter 3 and the supply chain handbook's Annex 3 ask the same three questions of each bottleneck (impact on the process, likelihood of overcoming it, importance to a wide range of stakeholders) and differ from this platform's DIIG methodology only in what they do with the answers. Both are on record; neither replaces the other.

**Alternative A: Score each criterion 1-3, add the scores, rank by total.**

> "Formula for scoring and ranking bottlenecks, with examples."<br>— DIIG Table 3.3.1, PDF p.50 (printed p.38) (`9789240010567-eng/page-050`)

> "Adding the scores yields the prioritized ranking."<br>— SC Annex 3, Template for prioritizing DHSC challenges, PDF p.68 (`9789240101197-eng/page-068`)

**Alternative B: Answer each criterion with its reason, and order by argument; print no score.**

> "adopts the three criteria and refuses the arithmetic"<br>— `smart-base/methodologies/diig.md`, §"Never quantify a judgement to make it look measured — and here is where"

*diig.md's refusal stands as written. The summed score is recorded beside it as the sources' own alternative, not adopted and not rejected here.*

## What "actor" means, and what each layer could change

Three bodies of work use "actor", and they do not mean the same thing. The Reference Architecture itself uses it in two senses. Read against folio-assistant's role model, the RA's conformance actor (§3.7.2) and SMART's generic persona are ROLES (something a participant plays), while folio-assistant's actor is the PARTICIPANT that plays one. The RA's §4.3.2 sense sits between the two: it names human and system participants together with "the roles they play", which is folio-assistant's split, under one word.

### Reference Architecture, conformance model (§3.7.2, §3.7.6)

An abstract information-processing role, in the IHE sense: a named set of responsibilities, independent of any product. It is modelled as an ArchiMate Application Component; a concrete system is a separate Application Component that realises it. One system may realise several actors, and one actor may be realised by many systems. Conformance is claimed by a system for an actor.

> "An actor is an abstract information-processing role"<br>— RA §3.7.2 The model, PDF pp.90-94 (`who-dpi-h-reference-architecture-draft-v1/sec-048-372-the-model`)

> "the system realises the actor"<br>— RA §3.7.2 The model, PDF pp.90-94 (`who-dpi-h-reference-architecture-draft-v1/sec-048-372-the-model`)

> "Application Component (system in an actor role)"<br>— RA §3.7.6, Table 3.7.2, PDF pp.97-99 (`who-dpi-h-reference-architecture-draft-v1/sec-052-376-constructs-and-their-counterparts`)

### Reference Architecture, implementation guidance (§4.3.2)

The human and system participants in a transaction, named together with the roles they play, and governed as a reusable role schema per DPI-H component (for a registry: the registrant, the verifying authority, the consuming system). This section cites the SMART Guidelines' generic personas and actor definitions as its worked example.

> "the actors — both human and system — that participate in each transaction, and the roles they play"<br>— RA §4.3.2 Actors and roles: defining who participates, PDF pp.106-107 (`who-dpi-h-reference-architecture-draft-v1/sec-063-432-actors-and-roles-defining-who-participates`)

> "WHO SMART Guidelines offer a worked example of this practice."<br>— RA §4.3.2, PDF pp.106-107 (`who-dpi-h-reference-architecture-draft-v1/sec-063-432-actors-and-roles-defining-who-participates`)

### SMART Guidelines / DAK (generic personas, ActorDefinition)

A DAK's generic persona is a depersonalised, context-free description of a human or system actor; the L3 implementation guide expresses each persona as a FHIR ActorDefinition, constrained by SMART Base's SGActor profile. Both are role descriptions: no persona is a particular person or deployed system.

> "Depiction of the human and system actors."<br>— `smart-base/fhir-artifact-index/index.json`, StructureDefinition/GenericPersona, description

> "Structure and constraints for ActorDefinition resources used in SMART Guidelines"<br>— `smart-base/fhir-artifact-index/index.json`, StructureDefinition/SGActor, description

> "depersonalised, context-free descriptions of the human and system actors"<br>— RA §4.3.2, PDF pp.106-107, describing the DAK (`who-dpi-h-reference-architecture-draft-v1/sec-063-432-actors-and-roles-defining-who-participates`)

### folio-assistant role model

A concrete participant, human, agentic or mechanical, that persists across every process. It takes on a Role, which is the BPMN swimlane; the role carries the skills. The RA's conformance actor and a DAK persona correspond to folio-assistant's ROLE; the RA's "system realising an actor", and the participants of RA §4.3.2, correspond to folio-assistant's ACTOR (a mechanical one, for a system) taking on that role.

> "A concrete participant, human, agentic or mechanical, that persists across every process and takes on roles."<br>— `folio-assistant-core/glossary/cat-harness.glossary.json`, term "actor"

> "a persona an actor *takes on* because of the lane it is acting in"<br>— `cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/role-model.md`, §"Roles are swimlanes", the objects table

### The same three ideas, side by side

| idea | RA (draft) | SMART Guidelines / DAK | folio-assistant |
|---|---|---|---|
| a named set of responsibilities, independent of who fulfils it | actor (§3.7.2); role (§4.3.2) | generic persona; ActorDefinition | role (swimlane) |
| the concrete thing that fulfils it | system realising an actor (§3.7.6); human or system participant (§4.3.2) | not modelled (a DAK stays depersonalised) | actor (human, agentic or mechanical) |
| the binding between the two | Realisation (system → actor) | none in the DAK; an implementation's own deployment | an actor takes on a role for the duration of a lane |

### Changes, one per layer

Owner, 2026-10-03: "1. F-A mapping, 2. Draft RA comment, 3. SMART Base proposal"

- **Reference Architecture (draft)** (*drafted for the owner to send; not sent*): Qualify the two senses. §3.7.2 and Table 3.7.2 already say "abstract role"; §4.3.2 uses "actor" for the participant and pairs it with "role". A glossary entry for actor (the draft's glossary has none; the term is defined only in the body) naming the conformance sense as primary, and §4.3.2 saying "participants" where it means the human and system parties, would remove the ambiguity. This is a comment on a public-comment DRAFT, for WHO to take or leave. **Outcome:** A public comment on the DRAFT is written, citing its line and page numbers. The owner sends it; nothing has been posted. See [`smart-base/findings/ra-actor-comment.md`](ra-actor-comment.md).
- **folio-assistant** (*applied in this repository*): Keep folio-assistant's "actor" as settled by role-model, and record the mapping rather than the WHO wording: when an RA or SMART term is ingested, an RA actor or a DAK persona maps to a folio-assistant ROLE (closeMatch), never to an actor, and the RA's realising system maps to a mechanical actor. Concretely: a closeMatch from the glossary's role entry to the RA's conformance actor and to SMART's GenericPersona, and a sentence in role-model saying so. **Outcome:** The glossary's role entry now carries a closeMatch to the RA §3.7.2 section and to SMART Base's GenericPersona, and role-model says an RA actor or a DAK persona maps to a Role, never an Actor. See [`folio-assistant-core/glossary/cat-harness.glossary.json`](../../folio-assistant-core/glossary/cat-harness.glossary.json), [`cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/role-model.md`](../../cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/role-model.md).
- **SMART Guidelines / SMART Base** (*drafted for the owner to send; not sent*): State, in SMART Base's GenericPersona or SGActor description, that a persona is a role and that a system persona (DAK.Persona.System.*) is realised by the systems an implementation deploys: the RA §3.7.2 realisation relationship. That ties the DAK's personas to the RA's conformance model, which §4.3.2 already points at, without renaming anything. A proposal for the upstream IG, not an edit to the ingested copy, which is read-only here. **Outcome:** An issue for the upstream SMART Base IG is written. The owner files it; nothing has been filed, and the read-only ingested copy is unchanged. See [`smart-base/findings/smart-base-persona-issue.md`](smart-base-persona-issue.md).

## Terms defined differently

40 terms carry more than one definition across the sources: 10 with a different meaning or an added claim (**substantive**), 4 defined two ways inside one source (**internal**), and 26 that differ only in wording. A term is listed under the most severe difference it has. In each table, row A is the first source in the order PHC, SC, PC, RA; that order is a reading order, not a ranking.
